claim_being_audited: The model may be certified for deployment on the current record only if the audit packet discloses the unresolved small-business onboarding limitation; the evidence does not support a clean claim that no material limitations exist or that mitigation is fully approved.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence supports both certification and the absence of unresolved material limitations or shows an approved mitigation satisfying policy requirements.
Use compliant_with_caveats if admissible evidence supports launch readiness overall but only with explicit disclosure or follow-up documentation caveats.
Use suspicious if the packet overclaims beyond the admissible record or leaves the policy predicate unresolved while still implying clean support.
Use noncompliant if the record contradicts certification or lacks any plausible policy-compliant basis.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance, if one exists, covering the small-business onboarding limitation before launch.
A finalized mitigation/runbook with accountable owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
A documented materiality determination for the small-business onboarding gap tied to the named launch use case.
specific_concerns: The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation record because the owner and alert threshold remain TBD, and the policy text also requires review date and rollback criterion for a no-caveat certification basis.
The model-card draft states there are no known material limitations while the record contains an unresolved below-target launch-use-case slice.
The admissible record supports disclosure of the remaining limitation more clearly than it supports any claim that the limitation is immaterial.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that there are no known material limitations.
Any claim that the mitigation artifact is complete or approved.
Any claim that certification without caveats is supported by the current record alone.
